claim: fullWindowCount is declared inside the step loop but assigned only inside the `if ts == ev.startTimestamp || selVS.Timestamp == nil` block, so for @-anchored range selectors every step after the first contributes 0 to TotalSamples/IncrementSamplesAtStep (previously the live floats/histograms slices reused across steps were counted). This silently changes existing totalQueryableSamples, totalQueryableSamplesPerStep and prometheus_engine_query_samples_total; reachable via multi-argument range functions (quantile_over_time, predict_linear, double_exponential_smoothing) since single-argument calls are masked by StepInvariantExpr. Measured 20 -> 8, per-step [5 5 5 5] -> [5 1 1 1] vs base commit.
raw: #1 🟠 High: `TotalSamples` silently stops counting per-step for `@`-anchored range selectors

claim: evalSubquery merges the child's SamplesRead into the parent via MergeSamplesReadFromSubquery, and the resulting synthetic matrix is then counted again by the range-vector branch's IncrementSamplesReadAtStep at engine.go:2184, so SamplesRead / prometheus_engine_query_samples_read_total is ~2x for any query with a subquery (rate(m[5m:1m]): TotalSamples=5, SamplesRead=10). samplesRead can exceed totalQueryableSamples, contradicting the docs added at docs/querying/api.md:246 and docs/feature_flags.md:47 ('For other query types, this equals totalQueryableSamples'); the change's own test table records SamplesRead: 2 vs TotalSamples: 1 and SamplesRead: 102 vs TotalSamples: 78.
raw: #2 🟠 High: `SamplesRead` double-counts every subquery, and the documented invariant it advertises is false

claim: NewChildWithStepTracking calls InitStepTracking, which allocates both TotalSamplesPerStep and SamplesReadPerStep, but only SamplesReadPerStep is consumed for subquery children (TotalSamples is folded into the parent as a scalar at engine.go:2424; MergeSamplesReadFromSubquery does not touch totals) — every subquery evaluation under promql-per-step-stats allocates and writes a dead []int64 (callers engine.go:1869, :2397) where NewChild() previously allocated nothing.

claim: outerStep = numOuterSteps - 1 could index SamplesReadPerStep[-1] when the parent array is empty; considered false because InitStepTracking only yields numSteps < 1 if start-end >= interval and eval returns early at engine.go:1928 when endTimestamp < startTimestamp, so numSteps never drops below 1 (10 degenerate shapes probed, no panic).
raw: [false] `outerStep = numOuterSteps - 1` indexing `SamplesReadPerStep[-1]` when the parent array is empty

claim: Possible division by zero in InitStepTracking when interval == 0; considered false because instant queries use interval: 1 (engine.go:805) and subquery intervals come from a non-zero e.Step or noStepSubqueryIntervalFn.

MergeSamplesReadFromSubquery could merge misaligned per-step indices; considered false because the child is built with the parent's (start, end, interval) and the inner SubqueryExpr merge writes using the parent's startTimestamp/Interval, so index i means the same step on both sides.

IncrementSamplesReadAtStep guards i < len but not i >= 0, diverging from IncrementSamplesAtStep which has no bounds check at all; no call site produces a negative index (step starts at -1 and is incremented before first use), so the asymmetry is cosmetic.
raw: [minor] `IncrementSamplesReadAtStep` guards `i < len` but not `i >= 0`, diverging from `IncrementSamplesAtStep`
